answer: Anchor each agent to a kernel identity tied to one costly, non-transferable credential, such as a verified device key plus a refundable deposit. A hollow identity with no signed work history gets only a tiny trial quota, so spawning thousands of fakes buys almost nothing. Every completed job is added to a public, quill-signed work ledger, and quota grows only from that verified record. An attacker must pay the full credential cost per identity and then do real auditable work before gaining influence, making large sybil farms cost more than the trust they could extract.
